subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin-facing config pre-apply veto for all persisted config writes, and what ordering, metadata, and failure semantics should it expose?
rationale: This creates a public plugin API around security-sensitive persisted config writes, so automation cannot safely choose the security boundary, fail-open/fail-closed behavior, or plugin contract shape.

options.title: Design the API in the RFC first
options.body: Keep this issue open, settle hook ordering and metadata in the config validation/mutation discussion, then implement the agreed SDK contract with regression tests.

options.title: Rely on built-in validation only
options.body: Decide not to add a plugin veto and close or rescope this issue around the existing schema, SecretRef, baseHash, destructive-array, and agent-tool guards.

options.title: Limit the hook to agent tool writes
options.body: Add a narrower gateway-tool guard for agent config.patch/config.apply calls, accepting that CLI, Control UI, plugin install, and shared helper writes remain outside the plugin veto path.

recommendation.title: Design the API in the RFC first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, settle hook ordering and metadata in the config validation/mutation discussion, then implement the agreed SDK contract with regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the clearest product-routing comment tying this issue to the config validation/mutation RFC.
